annotations.title: What depositors kept, against what was advertised

description: What depositors actually KEPT, against what their vault advertised. READ `population` BEFORE QUOTING ANY SHARE FROM THIS. The comparison covers only the vaults where we hold BOTH an advertised rate and a realised one, which is a narrow and lopsided set, usually dominated by one venue: `population.largestVenue` names it and `population.concentration` says how much of the set it is. A share from here is a statement about those vaults, never about DeFi and never about this whole site. Not the vault’s return, which is what a unit held throughout would have earned: this is read from the depositor register, per vault, and set against the venue’s own quote scaled to how long those depositors have held. Measured today: of the vaults with a comparison, four in five gave their depositors less, at a median of thirty points short. ADVERTISED RATES ARE DECIMAL FRACTIONS and some are in the hundreds of per cent: 0.042 is 4.2% and 4.2 is 420%. Those survive a stated band of -1 to 5 (-100% to 500%); `advertisedBand.refused` says how many readings the band threw out, and `advertisedIsHigh` marks each row above 100% so a remarkable figure cannot be mistaken for a misplaced decimal. TWO THINGS TO REPEAT WHENEVER QUOTING IT. A depositor who withdrew everything is not in the register and the ones who left after losing are exactly the ones a return figure most needs, so this reads BETTER than the truth rather than worse; and `gapPoints` is percentage POINTS, not per cent, because a depositor cannot lose more than they put in. The aggregate and the widest gaps are free; the rest of the list needs the earned.detail capability and `withheld` says how many are missing.
name: vaults_earned

advertisedBand.description: minDecimal, maxDecimal, refused and means. Advertised rates are decimal fractions, so a value above 1 is above 100%; readings outside the band are refused rather than counted as zero.

comparable.description: Vaults where the two sides can be set against each other at all. This is the population every share here is over.

items.description: name, slug, venue, advertised, advertisedIsHigh, kept, gapPoints, medianDaysHeld. Widest gap first.

limits.description: What this cannot tell you, including the survivorship inside the register. Quote it with the numbers.

losingShare.description: Measured depositors who are down, as a decimal fraction.

population.description: Who the comparison is actually about: listed, comparable, byVenue, largestVenue, concentration and isOneVenue. `listed` is how many survived the advertised band and are in `byVenue`; `comparable` is the job own count. They are different counts and must never be divided into one another. Where isOneVenue is true the figure is a reading about that one venue in a market-wide sentence.

shortOfAdvertised.description: Of those, how many gave their depositors less.

shortOfAdvertisedShare.description: The headline share, as a decimal fraction. Never quote it without `population` beside it.

withheld.description: Rows the plan does not carry. Zero with earned.detail.
